questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I liked the fact that it was the oldest university in the Global North. It really mattered to me, that I could get the Erasmus + grant, so it had to be within Europe. Thirdly, it is nice that the weather is good and the food is wonderful.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually okay. You just need to find the right email for the questions for Erasmus students, so look out for that, they are very helpful once you find it. The only BIG problem is, that the way you apply for courses are very different and not at all informed beforehand. You have to be very open the first few weeks, and go to all kinds of courses and hope you can apply for one of them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Did not really recieve anything, there is nothing planned for exchange students. They really need to get better at this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's hard, you need to get a hold of Leonardi Sardini's company, they can help you, but it is really expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't be too concerned with "living inside the walls", it is nice to be close yes, but it is SUPER touristy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is so hard to understand how to sign up for courses, at least compared to UCPH

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember it clearly, but you have to make a video call to check in when you arrive, this was very easy and they emailed you about this beforehand. Just do it as soon as you arrive in Italy, not when you arrive in Bologna. But I did it 2 weeks late and they were very sweet. The big problem is the courses. You have to email the professor or whatever for each course and ask them if there are any requirements to sign into their course. Then you just use a guide they provide to sign up for it online. But sign up to anything you might consider, then you can just remove them if you don't want it or don't get in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, they guide you on how to sign up for courses and make an OLA, which you need to make like 2 months beforehand, on the day you start taking courses. So it's a bit late. But check the guides online, they work fine.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went fine in the end!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make the OLA as soon as you can based on the old courses, because you have to revise it anyways. Don't get freaked out, they are very chill with exams, and if you mail them, they are really helpful and forgiving. But sign up for all the courses you consider, you can always cancel it, so please don't hesitate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is fine. Im from UCPH, and if you want to learn something take MA programmes. The others are just boring and with a lot of tests. Masters are interesting and usually simpler exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different I guess. Many of them sit while teaching. The exams can be taken on different dates over the span of half a year. The readings a not set for each class, but are just posted un-chronologically?? So make your own reading list, so you dont have to read like 10 books in the exam period. And they also have a lot of courses that are only 5 weeks, I would recommend doing those, they are nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Atlantic and Global History of Modern Political Concepts
Geography and Cognition of European Territories
Political Ecology of Work
Visualizing the Italian Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Atlantic and Global History of Modern Political Concepts & Geography and Cognition of European Territories, were both amazing. Number two was a bit hard to grasp, but just go with the flow. The first one was just epic, he is really cute and intelligent

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Restaurants, they are good and comparatively cheap, but if you go out to eat a lot, it will cost you a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fet cheese is expensive. All drinks are super cheap. Food is ok, not really that cheap, exept some vegetables are like super cheap, and fish.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a gym but you needed doctors certificate and it was not even very cheap

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Bring your bike, they have the most beautiful scenic biking routes you could ever imagine. It is the perfect way to discover small hidden countryside towns and to explore the landscape, while getting a workout and fleeing the pollution and noise of the city.
Go to the cinemas, they are epic, especially Modernissimo and Lumiere!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to a football game. Go to San Siro and spend a night in Milan. Visit Modena for the food marked, its 5 euros with train. Visit Florence or Venice. I dont know... I did no leave the city that much, they have so many nice places: Labas, Kinotto, Salomé Salomé. I would go get some drinks and some friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, they are nice and fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do it in class breaks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: walking on the street. They walk in front of you, and never give other people space.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Staying outside, all the time, even in minus degrees.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring your bike. Look at churches. Befriend your teacher.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress it, they won't.

Find an appartment with access to light

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: being relaxed.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Becoming friends with the locals, but then again, I did not really try that hard. And honestly don't, cause you are only there for half a year. I think it will happen if it happens. I got some nice friends from Italy, but not from Bologna.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
